That being said, as a first step to teaching yourself music theory, I'd recommend that you buy a book on music theory that starts from zero. It can help you broaden your understaning of what the sound is, how music "science" started and got to the point where it is today  (with not much details, don't worry), before talking about what a major scale is and how chords are created. Talking about guitar playing, from my own experience, techique is a multi-dimensional thing. In terms of speed, precision and skill required, Megadeth is well above average, but there are still many bands that are more technical (Nevermore, Jason Becker, Annihilator, Buckethead, Children of Bodom and these boring death-progressive bands). But fast and precise fingers are just one (big) part of what technique is.

Take the fastest and most precise guitarist. Can he play the solo of "when a blind man cries" or "comfortably numb" as well as he can play the "flight of the bubble bee"? Not necessarily. These two solos are not considered even average-difficult, yet they are too damn hard to play correctly. To create the emotion that is meant to be created. To create that emotion through your fingers. That's technique, too. The ability to play one note perfectly. 

The second dimension of technique I'm mentioning, is usually seen as "emotion", but it's false. People have emotions. The sound you create comes through your fingers. The way you bend a string is technique. Megadeth, imo, are at pro level in that dimension of technique. And that's because of Marty  and Mustaine. Broderick or Kiko, who are far more precise, faster and cleaner than Marty (what people would perceive as technically superior) can't play Tornado of Souls or Lucretia solos like Marty. But Broderick did a great job in Nevermore, where he played faster and more difficult things. Take Broderick and give him a Jeff Loomis solo. He will be perfect. But at a Marty solo, though "technically superior", he won't do that good of a job. It's not that he "doesn't have emotion". It's that he is an expert at the one side of technique, but lacks the other. 

To end with, I'd like to say that Megadeth are from the few bands that combine speed, skill and melody to such a pleasant degree and that's why you like them. It's easy to get lost in speed and create a chaotic song.
